parsed.doc_summary: San Diego Municipal Code Ch. 9, Art. 8, Div. 7 (Residential Tenant Protections): just-cause eviction requirements, no-fault relocation assistance (2 months' rent, 3 for seniors/disabled), notice rules, buyout rules, retaliation ban, remedies. Effective 2023-06-24.

rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections (Tenants' Right to Know)
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot terminate a tenancy without just cause (at-fault or no-fault). For no-fault terminations the landlord must give 30/60 days' written notice with the basis, pay relocation assistance of 2 months' rent (3 months if tenant is a senior or disabled) or waive that rent, and offer to re-rent for five years in some cases. Retaliation is prohibited and violations can void the notice and bring treble damages.
citation_aliases: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; no-fault relocation = 2 months' rent (3 for seniors/disabled)
rules.effective_date_note: Division as retitled/amended by O-21647 N.S., effective 6-24-2023; amended by O-21769 N.S. effective 2024-03-28.
rules.exemptions: Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8); mobilehomes under MRL; hotels/short-term; care facilities and transitional housing; dormitories; shared kitchen/bath with owner-occupant; owner-occupied single-family or duplex; housing with certificate of occupancy within previous 15 years; separately alienable property owned by non-REIT/corporation/LLC-with-corporate-member landlord with written notice.
rules.penalty: Wrongful eviction damages of at least 3x actual economic damages; at least 3x relocation assistance owed; attorney's fees in court's discretion; punitive damages; notice void; city enforcement.
rules.interaction: Consistent with and in addition to Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2.

unverifiable_exemptions: separately alienable property owned by non-corporate landlord with written notice
dormitories, care facilities, transitional housing, mobilehomes
